- When sentiment shows strong bullish (1.00) or bearish (-1.00) signals in recent days, model tends to overreact — especially after spikes — and forecasts overshoot or undershoot the true trend.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; true values often dip below forecast.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects with a steep drop in forecast, but true price usually rebounds slightly before settling.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00), model tends to forecast mean-reversion patterns too aggressively, leading to premature corrections.
- Model underestimates true price in the final 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is bearish or neutral — likely due to lag in capturing sentiment-driven sell-off.
- If sentiment turns bearish after a recent peak, model often fails to adjust forecast downward quickly — true price drops faster than forecasted.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in the last 3–5 days of the 18-day history, leading to delayed correction in forecasts.
- When sentiment is consistently bullish over 3+ days, model often forecasts a sustained rise, but true price often corrects mid-horizon — suggesting model overestimates momentum.
